reviewed_content.statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

An algebraic space $X$ is decent if every point $x\in|X|$ admits a quasi-compact representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is reasonable if every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has universally bounded finite fibres, and very reasonable if it is Zariski-locally covered by quasi-compact surjective étale schemes. A morphism $f:X\to Y$ is *decent* (respectively reasonable, very reasonable or with property $(\beta)$) if $X\times_YT$ has that property for every scheme $T\to Y$. Property $(\beta)$ for a space means that every point can be represented by a monomorphism from a field spectrum.

For decent $X$ and $x\in|X|$, $\kappa(x)$ is the field associated with the representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. An *elementary étale neighborhood* $(U,u)\to(X,x)$ is an étale scheme chart whose pointed field map $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to X$ is such a monomorphism. Its henselian local ring is $\mathcal O_{X,x}^{h}=\varinjlim_{(U,u)}\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ over the cofiltered category of elementary étale neighborhoods, and it agrees with $\mathcal O_{U,u}^h$ for any one of them. A decent space's point-set $|X|$ is sober and admits a dense open schematic locus when it has finitely many irreducible components.

An algebraic space $X$ is *Jacobson* if it admits an étale surjective cover by Jacobson schemes. A topological space $|X|$ is Jacobson if closed points are dense in every closed subset. A *finite type point* $x\in X_{\mathrm{ft\text{-}pts}}$ is a point represented by a morphism from a field spectrum locally of finite type over $X$. A decent locally Noetherian algebraic space has a sober underlying topological space, and its specialization relations agree locally with those on elementary étale scheme charts.

Any algebraic space locally of finite type over $X$ is Jacobson.

\label{lemma-Jacobson-ft-points-lift-to-closed}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be a Jacobson algebraic space over $S$.
For $x \in X_{\text{ft-pts}}$ and $g : W \to X$ locally of finite type
with $W$ a scheme, if $x \in \Im(|g|)$, then there exists a closed
point of $W$ mapping to $x$.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-punctured-spec}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be a decent locally Noetherian algebraic
space over $S$. Let $x \in |X|$. Then
$$
W = \{x' \in |X| : x' \leadsto x,\ x' \not = x\}
$$
is a Noetherian, spectral, sober, Jacobson topological space.
